summary: Implemented the ADR-028 clause 2 authoritative, code-evidenced restart-required set (goal G8, phase 16 task 16.2) and its testability. src/ArrTags/Configuration/SettingApplicationScope.cs, SettingClassification.cs, and RestartRequiredSettings.cs are the code-owned classification of all 43 user-adjustable settings (every writable property of PluginConfiguration, ArrConnectionConfiguration, OperationalLimits, RendererConfiguration, and BadgeSelectorConfiguration; BadgeSelectorConfiguration.Selector is the fixed code-owned selector and is not user-adjustable). Each entry records the binary scope, the mixed flag, the settings-page element id(s), and per-consumer code evidence; SettingClassification enforces the ADR invariants at construction (mixed must be restart-required, per-operation must have no construction capture evidence, restart-required needs evidence or a recorded note). The evidenced restart-required set is exactly seven settings: OperationalLimits.SourceArtifactLimitBytes, DerivedArtifactLimitBytes, and MaxImageDimensionPixels (each mixed: SourceArtifactStore/JellyfinArtworkImageAccess/ArtworkSourceReader, ArtworkPublisher, and ArtworkSourceReader capture at singleton construction while RenderLimitGuard re-resolves per render through the work item's snapshot.Limits), plus the construction-only RenderCacheTtlMinutes, RenderCacheQuotaBytes, and TerminalProvenanceRetentionDays (StateRepository) and ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes (SourceArtifactStore over the captured repository limits). Every other setting is per-operation. One audited finding is recorded rather than silently omitted: the global OperationalLimits.RequestTimeoutSeconds is validated, persisted, and displayed but has no runtime consumer; the effective timeout is the per-connection ArrConnectionConfiguration.RequestTimeoutSeconds, so the global field is classified per-operation with an explicit audit note and pinned as the only classified setting without a runtime consumer (it is not changed by this task). config.html gains the restartRequiredFields mirror (seven entries with setting, elementId, and mixed) after the byte-limit mapping, data only: 16.3 renders note text from it and 16.5 adds the modal; no note text, save-path, persisted-state, validation, endpoint, or dependency change is made. Tests: RestartRequiredSettingsTests (10 cases: exact restart-required set, exact mixed set with mixed=>restart-required, unique/consistent entries, the real capture type named by each restart-required entry, lookup, the inert setting, no-silent-member reflection over the five model types, the static page element per restart-required setting, exact page-mirror equality, and the constructor guard) and RestartRequiredConsumerEvidenceTests (7 cases: StateRepository TTL/terminal-retention behavior from the captured limits plus a value-lock that the captured limits do not track a replacement snapshot, SourceArtifactStore captured source limit and quota, ArtworkSourceReader captured byte and dimension limits, ArtworkPublisher captured derived limit, and LibraryWorkQueue/LogVerbosityGate per-operation resolution). interpretations.question: How should the global OperationalLimits.RequestTimeoutSeconds be classified when it has no runtime consumer at all?
interpretations.chosen: Per-operation, with no restart note, and an explicit audited note in the classification and the evidence doc recording that the field is inert and that the effective timeout is the per-connection ArrConnectionConfiguration.RequestTimeoutSeconds.
interpretations.basis: ADR-028 clause 2 defines the binary classification in terms of consumers: restart-required when any consumer resolves the value at singleton construction, per-operation when every consumer resolves it from the current snapshot per operation. With zero consumers, no construction capture exists, so the setting is not restart-required, and classifying it restart-required would be a false page claim (a restart would not apply it either). The finding is disclosed rather than silently omitted; the field is not changed.
interpretations.impact: Task 16.3 will render no restart note for this setting. The pre-existing inert field remains inert; changing or removing it is not assigned to any PLANS.md task and is recorded as an open follow-up. No persisted state, save path, or validation semantics change.

interpretations.question: What is the classification domain: only the OperationalLimits properties plus LogVerbosity, or every user-adjustable setting?
interpretations.chosen: Every writable property of the five configuration model types the settings page round-trips (PluginConfiguration, ArrConnectionConfiguration, OperationalLimits, RendererConfiguration, BadgeSelectorConfiguration): 43 settings.
interpretations.basis: ADR-028 clause 2 says 'the authoritative set of settings that require a host restart', and G8 requires every restart-required setting in the settings page to carry note text, so the set must cover every page-adjustable setting. DashboardSettingsPageTests already treats exactly those five types as the user-adjustable domain (and proves the page covers every writable property), so a newly added property is caught by the no-silent-member test.
interpretations.impact: The 19 non-limit settings (connection fields, badge/library scope, renderer configuration, LogVerbosity, webhook secret) are recorded per-operation with consumer evidence, so no restart-required setting can hide outside the operational limits. The classification file is larger than a limits-only list.

interpretations.question: How does task 16.3 get the classification when the page is a static embedded resource?
interpretations.chosen: Add the page-side restartRequiredFields mirror now (setting, elementId, mixed), data only, following the 16.1 byteLimitFields/ByteLimitUnits precedent, with a structural test that compares it to the code-owned set exactly.
interpretations.basis: The page cannot read C# at runtime; 16.1 established the mirrored-table pattern and its structural-test enforcement. The task explicitly allows a page-side mirror and requires the classification to be designed so 16.3 can render note text from it.
interpretations.impact: The page carries an inert JS array until 16.3 renders notes; the mirror test fails on any drift between the page and the code-owned set. No note text or modal behavior is implemented here.

interpretations.question: Should BadgeSelectorConfiguration.Selector be classified?
interpretations.chosen: No. Selector is the fixed code-owned selector enum (the page presents it as the row identity); it is not a user-adjustable field, so it is the one writable property deliberately excluded from the classification.
interpretations.basis: The page never writes Selector from user input; the selector names are the code-owned vocabulary. The classification domain is user-adjustable settings.
interpretations.impact: The reflection coverage test skips exactly this property with the documented reason; any other writable property must be classified.

known_limitations: The global OperationalLimits.RequestTimeoutSeconds has no runtime consumer: when an operator changes that field, neither the running plugin nor a host restart applies it; the effective request timeout is the per-connection Sonarr/Radarr RequestTimeoutSeconds. The field is recorded in the classification note and the 16.2 evidence and is deliberately not changed by this task. Changing or removing it is an open follow-up not assigned to any PLANS.md task.

The host-guarded suite was not executed because ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset in this environment; the default run reports the same 63 host-guarded skips as the baseline, and no host-guarded fact was changed by this task.

Sensitivity for StateRepositoryLimitsDoNotTrackAReplacementSnapshot was not shown by a runtime probe: its failure mode requires changing the StateRepository constructor contract (a compile-level failure). RenderCacheQuotaBytes has code evidence, the exact-set/capture-site tests, and this value-lock, while the other six restart-required settings also have behavioral capture probes.

The per-operation classification of settings other than LibraryWorkQueue.Capacity and LogVerbosityGate is evidenced by cited consumer sites and existing suite coverage, not by a dedicated mutation probe per setting. A future singleton that begins capturing a currently per-operation setting would not be detected automatically; ADR-028's consequence requires classifying any future limit when it is added.
